pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should a text be well punctuated?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. punctuate a given text using commas, apostrophes, and capital letters correctly
2. use an apostrophe, commas and capital letters appropriately in composition writing

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a given text and take note of the commas, apostrophes and capital letters used,
2. Discuss the role of capital letters as used in various words or sentences in the passage,
3. Punctuate a passage correctly using commas, apostrophes, or capital letters where necessary,
4. Write a short composition on scientific innovations using capital letters, commas and apostrophes correctly, 1. Why should a text be well punctuated? 2. How does wrong punctation affect writing? 20
5. Assess each other’s composition and discuss how the punctuation marks and capital letters have been used,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should a text be well punctuated?
2. How does wrong punctation affect writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
